children: The Congress-led UDF government in Kerala has ordered a police inquiry into an Enforcement Directorate (ED) report seeking action against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena and her husband, former Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas, in the CMRL-Exalogic case.

State Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the government had decided to entrust the Director General of Police (DGP) with an inquiry into the ED report after examining the legal opinion of the Advocate General. The Advocate General had left it to the State Police to decide the further course of action on the report.
Chennithala said he discussed the matter with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan before the decision was taken.

The ED has alleged that Vijayan received ₹3.28 crore from Cochin Minerals and Rutile Ltd (CMRL) as bribes in return for extending favours to the company. It has also alleged that ₹2.78 crore was paid to Veena’s now-defunct IT firm, Exalogic Solutions, without corresponding services being rendered.

The agency has further alleged that funds were routed abroad through hawala channels with the assistance of Riyas. Its allegations are contained in a 25-page report submitted to the State Police Chief under Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
The ED had sought registration of an FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act against Vijayan, Veena and Riyas, citing evidence gathered during its investigation.

Pinarayi Vijayan and the CPI(M) have rejected the allegations, describing the ED action and demands for an inquiry as politically motivated. Riyas has also denied the allegations, describing media reports as false and threatening legal action, while alleging that the claims were fabricated to defame him.
CPI(M) State Secretary M.V. Govindan accused the central agency of attempting to manufacture false narratives that would not gain traction in Kerala.

title: CMRL-Exalogic case: Keralam orders police enquiry into ED report
